newsitem.title: THAILAND: Computer failure halts Thai stocks trading.
newsitem.headline: Computer failure halts Thai stocks trading.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) halted trading in all shares several minutes after the opening due to the partial breakdown of its major computer trading system, a spokeswoman said on Monday.
"We halted trading in all shares this morning. There is a technical problem with our computer system," a SET spokeswoman told Reuters.
The trading halt comes just before key announcements by the central bank at 0400 GMT on new monetary and other finance sector measures.
The spokeswoman said technicians were trying to hastily repair the system, but she declined to specify when share trading would resume.
The SET index was down 9.02 points or 1.55 percent on the open on Monday amid sales of finance and bank stocks after Friday's collapse of a mega-merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc.
"The stock exchange halted trading after we started trading for about four minutes. There remains a number of selling orders by foroeign investors on the queue," said one broker at a local brokerage.

Other traders said they were annoyed at the computer breakdown as it came at a critical time for the market when the central bank was due to make announcements and just after the collapse of the mega-merger.
